title: an unsealed option hands devbin's own wrapper flags to its tool -- 0087's class at the site its fix missed
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 while 0113's consumer page for check was written, and driven by cc at 142763d.

An option with a config `run:` and no `log:` runs unsealed, and devbin's own wrapper flags reach its tool as arguments. Driven: `commands.check.options.bare.run: echo bare-ran` with no `log:`, then `bin/devbin check bare --purge`, prints `bare-ran --purge` at rc 0. The same option with `log: true` strips the flag and acts on it: `purged 0 old run file(s) ... (keeping the newest 5 run(s))`.

This is 0087's class at the one site its fix did not reach. 0087 made every sealed path split the wrapper flags off through gate_split_args. run_option's unsealed branch still ends `"${words[@]}" "$@"` (lib/resolve), and run_command's unsealed exec does the same. `--purge`, `--purge-only` and `--allow-empty` mean nothing without a seal, so the honest answers are to refuse them there, naming why, or to drop them with a word. Handing them to the tool is neither, and a tool that rejects an unknown flag fails for a reason the person did not cause.

## Resolution

Fixed at eee4ed0. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. An unsealed option or command splits its argv with gate_split_args and says what became of devbin's wrapper flags (--purge, --purge-only, --allow-empty). Inside `all` it drops them: run_all hands one argv to every option, so they were typed for the sealed options beside it. Named directly, it passes them to the tool, which may own them (git commit's --allow-empty), since devbin has no seal to spend them on. Either way stderr says so, "it was" for one flag and "they were" for more.
- THE DESIGN MOVED ON REVIEW. The first cut dropped the flags everywhere. cc's review found that dropping or refusing them outside `all` left a project no way to hand a tool its own flag, and this issue's text had offered only those two options.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. The reworked arms are red before 0122. W1-W5 are killed: dropped everywhere, passed everywhere, nothing said, run_all forgetting its marker, and the command site forgetting the word. On cc's plural note, P1 (always plural) and P2 (always singular) are killed as well.
- REVIEW. cc: sound.
- THE SUITE. The full suite on the series as it landed -- land018 at c130b3a, whose 27 series paths are byte-identical to the landed commits: 1..1653, 1653 ok, 0 not ok, 4 skips (127, 135, 624, 626), rc 0, 12:39:28Z to 13:11:35Z. Each commit passed the gate (guards, critic, doctor) as it landed.
